questions.question:
Arrange the following countries according to world map from East to West.

1. Canada 2. Japan 3. India 4. Uzbekistan 5. Germany 6. Malaysia
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

To arrange countries from East to West, you need to look at their longitudinal positions on the world map.

1. Japan - This is the easternmost country among the given options.

2. Malaysia - Moving west from Japan, Malaysia is the next country.

3. India - West of Malaysia, India comes next.

4. Uzbekistan - Further west from India is Uzbekistan.

5. Germany - West of Uzbekistan, we find Germany.

6. Canada - Finally, the westernmost country among these is Canada.

So, the order would be: **2, 6, 3, 4, 5, 1**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

questions.question:
The numbers in each set are related to each other in a certain way. (2, 8, 100), (7, 2, 81), (4, 7, ?)

Based on the relationship among the numbers in the first two sets, select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the third set.
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number + 2nd number)² = 3rd number.

Now,

For, (2, 8, 100)

⇒ (2 + 8)² = 10² = 100.

For, (7, 2, 81)

⇒ (7 + 2)² = 9² = 81.

Similarly, for (4, 7, ?)

**⇒ (4 + 7)² = 11² = 121.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some tables are chairs.

II. All desks are chairs.

III. No chair is a fan.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some desks are tables.

II. Some fans are desks.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d89100b8742120e287c0d76a9b8e647e2f3eff7c32a17c934daa31be116dfb7.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some desks are tables → Does not follow (As some tables are chairs and all desks are chairs. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. Some fans are desks → Does not follow (As all desks are chairs and no chair is a fan. As whole desks come in chairs which cannot be fan, therefore, some fans are desks is false.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Neither conclusion I nor II follows"

questions.question:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements.

**Statements:**

All boxes are squares.

All squares are rectangles.

All rectangles are figures.

**Conclusions:**

I. All boxes are figures.

II. All squares are figures.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec03c5b7565e0acd3dfe858092571baf63b96d72c3179fa6810b4e9e91a67a75.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All boxes are figures → Follow (As all boxes are squares, all squares are rectangles and all rectangles are figures. As whole boxes comes in squares which whole comes in rectangles which whole comes in figures, therefore all boxes are figures is true.)

II. All squares are figures → Follow (As all squares are rectangles and all rectangles are figures. As whole squares comes in rectangles which whole comes in figures, therefore all squares are figures is true.)

∴ Here, Both conclusions I and II follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "**Both conclusions I and II follow**"
